limitations: Recorded gradient_norm is the global preclip parameter L2 norm; clipped fraction is determined from threshold1.0 in recipe_v2.py, not from separately recorded postclip norms.
A small clipping multiplier does not imply the adaptive optimizer makes an equally small parameter update. Muon orthogonalization, Adam moments, momentum and weight decay alter that relationship.
No per-parameter actual update metrics were recorded in these RecipeV2 logs; historical optimizer direction or per-loss update attribution cannot be reconstructed from these JSONL records alone.

Loss values and gradient norm shares are measured on different changing training batches. Parent and continuation windows are not matched audio; raw loss means are descriptive, not heldout quality rankings.
Shares are norms before summation at audio, not parameter update shares. Scale-bound saturation and global parameter-gradient clipping are different mechanisms.
Source file hashes establish which logs were analyzed, but this is not an independent proof that logged values exactly reflect every historical kernel operation.

Across the full parent history, the adversarial and feature-matching summaries cover only their active steps while reconstruction covers all steps; their separately averaged shares should not be summed as if observation counts matched.
